name: Shechtman counts ten points
scope: The forbidden symmetry that rewrote the definition of a crystal. T1: on April 8, 1982, at the U.S. National Bureau of Standards near Washington, Israeli materials scientist Dan Shechtman aimed an electron beam at a rapidly cooled aluminium-manganese alloy and counted TEN bright points in a ring around the centre -- a symmetry crystallography said was impossible (the hook is the COUNT, not the date). T2: the rule he broke -- a crystal was DEFINED as a pattern that repeats, and a repeating tiling of space can only carry 2-, 3-, 4- or 6-fold symmetry; a kid can check the reason on a floor, because regular pentagons leave gaps and hexagons do not. T3: the reception -- his own research-group leader handed him a textbook and told him to go back and read it, then asked him to leave the group for bringing disgrace on it; the work finally ran in Physical Review Letters in 1984 with Ilan Blech, Denis Gratias and John Cahn. T4: the loudest opponent was the most decorated chemist alive -- two-time Nobel laureate Linus Pauling, who said in public 'There is no such thing as quasicrystals, only quasi-scientists,' argued the pattern was really multiple twinned crystals overlapping, and held that position until his death in 1994. T5a: the mechanism -- Roger Penrose's two rhombus tiles fill a plane forever with fivefold symmetry and NEVER repeat; a quasicrystal is the three-dimensional version, carrying long-range ORDER without periodicity, which is why the diffraction spots stay razor-sharp. T5b: the verdict -- in 1992 the International Union of Crystallography rewrote the official definition of 'crystal' around a sharp diffraction pattern instead of a repeating lattice, and Shechtman took the 2011 Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone. T5c: quasicrystal structures were later identified in natural material from the Khatyrka meteorite, so nature had been making them all along.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com) checked first; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Shechtman (April 8 1982 NBS observation, Al-Mn alloy, tenfold symmetry, 'go back and read the textbook' + asked to leave the group, Pauling quote, PRL vol 53 no 20 1984 with Blech/Gratias/Cahn, 1992 IUCr redefinition, 2011 sole Nobel in Chemistry). Primary for build stage: Shechtman, Blech, Gratias & Cahn, 'Metallic Phase with Long-Range Orientational Order and No Translational Symmetry', Phys. Rev. Lett. 53(20), 1984.
framing_note: REVERSAL flagship. T1 keys the COUNT (ten points where ten were forbidden), never a date or a 'who discovered'. Accuracy rail: Pauling's line is a documented public quote and must be used verbatim -- 'There is no such thing as quasicrystals, only quasi-scientists' -- and NO additional insult quotes may be invented; also, Shechtman was asked to leave his research GROUP, not fired from the Bureau of Standards, and the Khatyrka-meteorite and lab-notebook '10 Fold???' details must be re-verified at build time before a rung asserts them. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (a two-time Nobel laureate publicly calling him a quasi-scientist -- and being wrong). Distractor mine: the real rival explanations serious crystallographers offered -- multiple twinning, an amorphous metallic glass, an icosahedral-glass model, an electron-microscope artifact -- plus real adjacent names (Pauling, Cahn, Penrose, Bragg). Anti-restatement: never let the stem say 'a symmetry that cannot repeat' before asking why tenfold was forbidden; describe the ring of ten spots and let the rule be recalled knowledge. Lane border: the pure geometry of aperiodic tilings belongs to MATH -- science owns the diffraction evidence and the fight.

name: McClintock reads the speckled kernel
scope: The genome that moves, seen in corn before anyone could sequence anything. T1: through the 1940s at Cold Spring Harbor, Barbara McClintock read the behaviour of chromosomes off the SPECKLES on maize kernels -- a purple kernel streaked with colourless sectors told her a gene had been switched off and then switched back on partway through the kernel's growth (the hook: she watched a gene turn on and off inside a single seed). T2: she named the two elements behind it -- Dissociation (Ds), sitting on the short arm of chromosome 9 and breaking it there, and Activator (Ac), a separate element elsewhere on the chromosome without which Ds would not move at all; the amount of Ac tuned how speckled the kernel got. T3: the claim that offended orthodoxy -- genes were supposed to be fixed beads at fixed addresses on a map; McClintock said pieces of the genome MOVE, inserting and excising, and their movement is what controls which genes speak. T4: at the Cold Spring Harbor Symposium in June 1951 she laid out the evidence and met, in her own words, 'puzzlement, even hostility'; after a full account in Genetics in 1953 she stopped publishing detailed journal papers on transposition and reported her results instead in the Carnegie Institution's in-house year books. T5a: the vindication arrived from a different kingdom -- in the late 1960s and 1970s molecular biologists found jumping elements in BACTERIA, in yeast and in bacteriophage, and the maize lady's 'controlling elements' turned out to be everywhere. T5b: she took the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine as the sole laureate -- and the honest correction: she was never an unknown outsider, having been elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1944 (only the third woman) and made president of the Genetics Society of America in 1945; what was resisted was the IDEA, not the person. T5c: the scale rung -- transposable-element sequence makes up a very large fraction of the human genome, the descendants of exactly the thing she saw moving in corn.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Barbara_McClintock) checked first (Ac/Ds two-component system, Ds on short arm of chromosome 9, breakage-fusion-bridge cycle, 1950 PNAS 'The Origin and Behavior of Mutable Loci in Maize', 1953 Genetics paper, June 4-8 1951 Cold Spring Harbor Symposium, 1983 sole Nobel); corroborated at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_McClintock ('puzzlement, even hostility'; NAS 1944; GSA president 1945; transposons found in bacteria/yeast/phage late 1960s-early 1970s; Nathaniel Comfort, 'The Tangled Field' 2001, and Evelyn Fox Keller, 'A Feeling for the Organism' 1983).
framing_note: REVERSAL flagship carrying this sub-strand's most important ACCURACY rail: the popular 'ignored because she was a woman' version is CONTESTED -- Nathaniel Comfort's The Tangled Field (2001) documents that she was already an NAS member (1944) and GSA president (1945) and well regarded by peers, and that the myth was amplified by Keller's 1983 biography and by McClintock herself. The bank tells the corrected version and makes the correction its own rung (T5b). Second rail: she did NOT stop working or reporting -- she stopped publishing detailed journal accounts after 1953 and kept reporting in Carnegie Institution Year Books; never write 'she gave up'. Third rail: state the human-genome transposon fraction only as a range the build verifies, never a crisp invented percentage. Dinner-test payoff: T1 (she read a gene switching off and back on in the speckles of a corn kernel). Distractor mine: real rival ideas of the era -- position-effect variegation, 'unstable mutable genes', Lamarckian adaptive mutation, viral infection of the kernel -- plus real adjacent names (Rollins Emerson, Marcus Rhoades, George Beadle, Harriet Creighton). Anti-restatement: the stem shows the speckled kernel; the answer must be recalled, never deducible from a stem clause naming movement.

name: Wegener: the ridicule and the seafloor verdict
scope: How a rejected claim finally won -- keyed to the FIGHT and the EVIDENCE, not the map. T1: in 1912 a German METEOROLOGIST stood up in Frankfurt and told professional geologists that their continents had once been joined and had been moving ever since; the wrong-credential problem is the hook and was half the reason he was dismissed. T2: his case was never the coastline jigsaw -- everyone had noticed that. It was that the SAME fossils sit on opposite shores of an ocean: the small freshwater reptile Mesosaurus in Brazil and southern Africa, and the seed fern Glossopteris across five now-separated southern landmasses; plus glacier scratches in what is now tropical Africa and India, and tropical coal in the Arctic. T3: the objection that beat him was a FAIR one -- he had no force strong enough to shove continents through solid ocean floor. His proposed 'Polflucht' pole-fleeing force and tidal drag were calculated by physicists, Harold Jeffreys foremost, to be orders of magnitude too weak. Being right about WHAT happens is not the same as being right about WHY. T4: in November 1926 Wegener presented at an American Association of Petroleum Geologists symposium in New York and was rejected by every speaker but the chairman; as early as 1917 Max Semper had published a jeer asking that geology be spared any further honouring by him. T5a: the missing engine came from someone else and arrived too late for Wegener -- Arthur Holmes proposed in 1931 that heat-driven convection cells in the mantle could carry crust like a conveyor; Wegener had died on the Greenland icecap in November 1930. T5b: the verdict came off the OCEAN FLOOR, from data nobody had in his lifetime -- magnetometers towed behind ships found the seafloor striped in mirror-image bands of alternating magnetic polarity on both sides of the mid-ocean ridges (Vine, Matthews and Morley, 1963), exactly the record a spreading conveyor would print, and a result that could easily have come out asymmetric and killed the idea. T5c: today satellite geodesy MEASURES the Atlantic widening by a couple of centimetres a year -- the drift is no longer inferred, it is read off an instrument.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Alfred_Wegener) checked first (1912 Frankfurt lecture, 1915 Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane, Mesosaurus + Glossopteris + palaeoclimate evidence, rejection for lack of a driving mechanism, 1960s validation by seafloor spreading and magnetic reversals, death Nov 1930 on the Greenland icecap); corroborated at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Wegener (November 1926 AAPG New York symposium 'rejection from everyone but the chairman'; Max Semper's 1917 published jeer) and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_drift (missing driving force; Arthur Holmes 1931 mantle convection; Vine-Matthews-Morley papers 1959-1963).
framing_note: REVERSAL keyed to the FIGHT, because the geography bank already tours Pangaea, the plate boundaries and the fossil map. The steel-man rung (T3) is MANDATORY and is what makes this ladder honest: the geologists' central objection was correct -- Wegener's mechanism really was wrong. Accuracy rail: do NOT use the widely-repeated Rollin T. Chamberlin 'forget everything which has been learned in the last 70 years' line or the 'utter, damned rot' attribution unless the build verifies them in the 1928 AAPG symposium volume; the VERIFIED reception facts are the November 1926 AAPG New York symposium and Semper's 1917 jeer. Second rail: Holmes proposed convection in 1931, not 1929, and Wegener was already dead. Dinner-test payoff: T5b -- mirror-image magnetic stripes either side of a ridge. Distractor mine: the real fixed-continent alternatives serious geologists held -- sunken land bridges, isthmian links, a contracting Earth, an expanding Earth, geosyncline theory -- plus real names (Jeffreys, Holmes, Schuchert, Du Toit). Lane border: the PLACES belong to geography and the rock-dating to the deep-time strand; this ladder owns the ridicule and the test.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY bank -- its shipped 'how we know the map moves' Wegener ladder already covers the Pangaea fit, the fossil matches and the plate-boundary places; this ladder must key DIFFERENT facts (the 1926 AAPG rejection, the Polflucht/tidal mechanism failure, Holmes's 1931 convection, the 1963 magnetic-stripe test, modern geodetic measurement). Also check geography's mid-ocean-ridge and Greenland content for stray overlap.

name: Prusiner's infection with no genes
scope: An infectious agent that is only a shape. T1: in 1982 at UCSF, Stanley Prusiner announced that the disease agent he had spent years purifying out of infected hamster brains contained NO DNA and NO RNA, and he coined a word for it in Science -- prion, from proteinaceous infectious particle (the hook: something that spreads an infection without carrying a single gene of its own). T2: why that was heresy -- every known infectious agent from virus to bacterium carries nucleic-acid instructions, and the central dogma held that information runs DNA to RNA to protein, one way; a protein was supposed to be a product, never a self-copying agent. T3: the clue that started it was a MEASUREMENT nobody wanted to explain -- in the 1960s the radiobiologist Tikvah Alper had hit the scrapie agent with doses of ionising and ultraviolet radiation heavy enough to shred any DNA or RNA, and the agent stayed infectious. T4: the mechanism -- the prion protein exists normally in healthy brains as a coiled, alpha-helical form (PrP-C); the dangerous form (PrP-Sc) is the SAME molecule folded into flat beta sheets, and on contact it templates its neighbour into the same misfold, which is why it resists proteases and piles up as plaque. A shape, not a code, is what is copied. T5a: the opposition had a serious name and a serious argument -- Nobel laureate David Baltimore among others held that the missing nucleic acid was a purification artifact, a hidden virus too small or too shielded to detect. That is exactly the right skeptical move; it simply turned out to be wrong. T5b: the closing evidence -- purification of the protease-resistant PrP 27-30 fragment and cloning of the PrP gene in 1984-85, transgenic mice lacking the gene that could not be infected, and eventually infectious prions generated in a tube from recombinant protein alone. T5c: the family and the honest caveat -- kuru among the Fore of Papua New Guinea, scrapie in sheep, BSE in cattle and variant CJD in humans are one disease family, and Prusiner took the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine alone; the frontier claim that Alzheimer's and Parkinson's proteins spread by similar templating is a LIVE hypothesis, not a settled result.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Stanley_B._Prusiner) checked first (1972 CJD patient during residency; scrapie purification from Syrian hamster brains; UV/ionising-radiation resistance work of Tikvah Alper as the inspiration; 1982 Science paper coining 'prion'; PrP-C alpha-helical vs PrP-Sc beta-sheet templated conversion; PrP 27-30 purification 1984 and PrP gene cloning; 2004 synthetic-prion demonstration; David Baltimore named as a prominent skeptic arguing the missing nucleic acid was an artifact; prion-like hypotheses for Alzheimer's/Parkinson's as ongoing work); corroborated at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_B._Prusiner (1982 Science paper, sole 1997 Nobel, Prusiner's own 'truly heretical' remark, 1991 NYT 'Heretical Theory On Brain Diseases Gains New Ground').
framing_note: REVERSAL + MECHANISM. Accuracy rail (non-negotiable): 'no nucleic acid' means none is required for INFECTIVITY -- never write that prion diseases have nothing to do with genes, because the PrP gene is the host's own and inherited mutations cause fatal familial insomnia and some CJD. Second rail: David Baltimore's objection is presented as legitimate science steel-manned, never as villainy -- the sub-strand's whole point is that good objections are part of how a claim gets tested. Third rail: the prion-like spread of Alzheimer's/Parkinson's proteins must be flagged as a live hypothesis; do not let a distractor secretly be the truth there. Teach 'central dogma' and 'misfold' before testing them. Dinner-test payoff: T4 -- the thing that copies itself is a FOLD. Distractor mine: the real rival hypotheses serious virologists held -- a slow virus, a viroid, a 'virino' (a tiny nucleic acid wrapped in host protein), an undetected bacterium -- plus real names (Alper, Gajdusek, Baltimore, Griffith). Lane border: mad cow disease as a British food-policy and farming crisis is HISTORY's; the Fore ethnography is not the wonder here. Do NOT duplicate Barry Marshall -- he lives in the medicine sub-strand.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank may cover the 1980s-90s British BSE/mad-cow crisis as a government and food-policy episode; this ladder must key the protein-only mechanism, the radiation evidence and the scientific opposition, not the policy story.

name: Chandrasekhar's limit and Eddington's law of Nature
scope: A teenager finds a ceiling on stars, and the most famous astrophysicist alive ridicules it in public. T1: in 1930, on the steamship voyage from India to England, a nineteen-year-old named Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar filled his notebooks working out what happens to a burnt-out star -- and found a CEILING: above roughly 1.4 times the Sun's mass a white dwarf cannot hold itself up (the hook: the calculation was done at sea, by a teenager, before he had even started at Cambridge). T2: what props up an ordinary white dwarf is not heat, because the fuel is gone -- it is electron degeneracy pressure, a quantum rule forbidding two electrons from occupying the same state, so squeezed electrons shove back. T3: Chandrasekhar's addition was special relativity: as the electrons are crushed toward light speed their outward push stops growing fast enough to keep pace with gravity, so the support fails above a definite mass. T4: on 11 January 1935 at the Royal Astronomical Society in London he presented the result, and Arthur Eddington -- the most celebrated astrophysicist in the world, and until that morning his supporter -- rose immediately afterward and demolished it in front of the room. T5a: Eddington's published objection was a conviction, not a calculation: 'I think there should be a law of Nature to prevent a star from behaving in this absurd way' (The Observatory, 1935). What he found intolerable was the consequence -- nothing left to halt total collapse. T5b: privately, physicists including Niels Bohr, Wolfgang Pauli and Ralph Fowler judged Chandrasekhar correct, and stayed publicly silent because Eddington's authority made the fight unwinnable; a consensus can stay wrong for years without anybody lying. T5c: Chandrasekhar left the argument, moved to the University of Chicago in 1936, worked on other problems for decades, and shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics with William Fowler -- fifty-three years after the voyage. T5d: the ceiling turned out to be a doorway -- above the limit a core collapses to a neutron star or a black hole, and a white dwarf pushed over the limit detonates as a Type Ia supernova; because the trigger mass is nearly always the same, those explosions peak at nearly the same brightness, which is how astronomers now measure distances across the universe.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subrahmanyan_Chandrasekhar (1930 voyage and the degenerate-electron-gas calculation; Eddington booking a talk immediately after his to attack it; Rosenfeld, Bohr and Moller finding Eddington's arguments lacking; move to Chicago December 1936; half-share of the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics with William A. Fowler); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandrasekhar_limit (11 January 1935 RAS meeting; Eddington's remark 'I think there should be a law of Nature to prevent a star from behaving in this absurd way' as published in The Observatory, 1935; Bohr, Pauli and Fowler privately agreeing but publicly silent given Eddington's authority; ~1.4 solar masses; collapse to neutron star or black hole; Type Ia relevance). Grokipedia checked for this figure; corroboration above.
framing_note: REVERSAL plus the sub-strand's clearest lesson in how AUTHORITY, not evidence, can freeze a field. Accuracy rail: Eddington's line must be quoted verbatim and sourced to The Observatory (1935) -- and the ladder must NOT accuse him of bad faith or theft; he was sincere, public and wrong, and he had been Chandrasekhar's patron. Second rail: the 1983 Nobel was SHARED with William Fowler and its citation covers stellar structure and evolution broadly, not the mass limit alone -- do not write 'he won the Nobel for the limit'. Dinner-test payoff: T1 (a nineteen-year-old works out a law of stars on a boat) with T5d as the closer. Distractor mine: real rival positions of the day -- Eddington's own attempt to modify relativistic degeneracy, the standard belief that every star ends as a white dwarf, 'the star simply sheds enough mass first', Landau's independent neutron-core suggestion -- plus real names (Eddington, Fowler, Milne, Pauli, Bohr). Lane border: black-hole physics itself belongs to the astronomy/cosmology strand; here the wonder is the limit and the fight.

name: Bretz's outrageous flood
scope: A landscape that only a catastrophe can explain, and a discipline that had sworn off catastrophes. T1: eastern Washington is scarred by things nothing gradual can carve -- a dry waterfall hundreds of feet high and far wider than Niagara, canyons cut straight down into solid basalt, and gravel bars the size of hills. In the early 1920s a Chicago geologist named J Harlen Bretz walked it and concluded the only agent big enough was a flood (the hook: a waterfall with no water and no river to have made it). T2: why that was close to blasphemy -- geology's founding rule, uniformitarianism, said the slow processes we can watch today are the key to the past, and it had won that status in a long fight against Biblical-flood catastrophism; Bretz's claim smelled to his colleagues like theology sneaking back in. T3: on 12 January 1927 the Geological Society of Washington invited Bretz to the Cosmos Club in Washington DC, where he found a line of senior geologists waiting with slow alternatives -- he later called them the challenging elders. T4: the hole in his own case, and he knew it: a flood needs a source of water and he had none. The water was found by somebody else -- USGS geologist Joseph Pardee had mapped an ice-dammed glacial lake in Montana, Lake Missoula, holding a volume comparable to Lakes Erie and Ontario combined. T5a: the clinching evidence was a SHAPE -- giant current ripples, the ordinary sand ripple's monstrous cousin, tens of feet high and hundreds of feet apart, on the floor of the drained lake basin and the flood channels; ripples of that size can only be built by water running deep and fast. T5b: the ledger closed late -- in 1979, at the age of 96, Bretz received the Penrose Medal, geology's highest honour, and reportedly told his son that all his enemies were dead so he had no one left to gloat over; the modern reading is not one flood but dozens, as the ice dam re-formed and burst again and again.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Harlen_Bretz (1923 Channeled Scablands papers; the 'outrageous hypothesis' framing; 12 January 1927 Geological Society of Washington meeting with competing theories presented and Bretz's 'challenging elders' description; resistance rooted in unfamiliarity with the region, his junior standing, and fear of Biblical-flood catastrophism; Joseph Pardee's glacial-lake evidence and his constrained position; acceptance by the 1950s with satellite imagery and hydraulics work in the 1970s; 1979 Penrose Medal at age 96 and the reported 'all my enemies are dead' remark to his son). Grokipedia checked for this topic; Wikipedia corroboration above.
framing_note: REVERSAL in which the resistance had a PRINCIPLED reason -- teach uniformitarianism honestly and sympathetically before testing it, because the geologists were defending a rule that had genuinely earned its place, and that is what makes this ladder more than a hero story. Accuracy rail: the 'all my enemies are dead' line is REPORTED (to his son) and must be framed as reported, never as a documented public statement. Second rail: Pardee did not simply hand Bretz the answer -- he held lake evidence for years while constrained from advocating the flood reading; do not compress that into 'a colleague solved it for him'. Third rail: modern work says repeated outburst floods, not a single one. Dinner-test payoff: T5a -- current ripples the size of houses, visible from the air. Distractor mine: the real slow alternatives offered in 1927 -- ordinary glacial meltwater over long ages, wind-blown loess erosion, subglacial stream carving, normal river downcutting over millions of years. Lane border: geography tours the Scablands and Dry Falls as PLACES; this ladder owns the 1927 argument, the missing water source and the ripple evidence.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY bank may cover the Channeled Scablands, Dry Falls or Glacial Lake Missoula as landscape/place content; keep every rung here on the reception, the objection, the missing-water-source problem and the giant-current-ripple test rather than the scenery tour.

name: Boltzmann, the atom, and the gravestone
scope: The man who said heat is just motion, and entropy is just counting. T1: in the 1870s Ludwig Boltzmann argued that the heat in a gas is nothing but the motion of countless invisible particles -- and that the reason a smashed egg never unsmashes is not a law forbidding it but a COUNT: the scrambled arrangements outnumber the tidy ones so overwhelmingly that tidy never comes back by accident. T2: the formula he is buried under. Entropy S equals k times the logarithm of W, where W is the number of microscopic arrangements that look identical from outside; the equation is carved on his gravestone in Vienna's Zentralfriedhof. (Teach W before testing it.) T3: his opponents were not cranks -- Ernst Mach and Wilhelm Ostwald led the 'energetics' school, which held that physics should speak only of measurable energy and that unobservable atoms were a convenient fiction. Their objection was about what counts as evidence, and in 1890 it was a reasonable question. T4: the attacks that hurt were mathematical, not philosophical -- Loschmidt's reversibility objection (Newton's laws run just as well backwards, so where does one-way time come from?) and Zermelo's recurrence objection. Boltzmann's answer reshaped the second law itself: entropy decrease is not forbidden, only astronomically improbable. T5a: the vindication he did not live to see -- Einstein's 1905 paper showed that the random jitter of a pollen grain in water is the visible fingerprint of molecular collisions, and Jean Perrin's 1908-09 measurements of that jitter yielded Avogadro's number and effectively ended the argument. T5b: the honest-caveat rung -- Boltzmann took his own life at Duino near Trieste on 5 September 1906, and the popular story that despair over the atom fight killed him is a STORY, not a documented finding; a long-standing severe depression is independently recorded. The bank says plainly that no one can settle the cause.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Boltzmann (S = k log W on the gravestone at Vienna's Zentralfriedhof and its microstate interpretation; Mach and Ostwald leading 'energetics' against atomism; death by suicide 5 September 1906 at Duino near Trieste with a documented severe neurasthenia/possible bipolar diagnosis and NO explicit documentary link to the atomism dispute; Einstein's 1905 Brownian-motion work and Perrin's 1908-09 colloid experiments confirming the Boltzmann and Avogadro constants). Grokipedia checked for this figure; corroboration above. Loschmidt and Zermelo objections to be re-verified at build time.
framing_note: REVERSAL + MECHANISM, and this sub-strand's key HONEST-CAVEAT ladder. Accuracy rail (non-negotiable): do NOT assert that Boltzmann killed himself because his atomic theory was rejected -- it is repeated everywhere and is not documented; his depression is recorded independently, and T5b must present the uncertainty AS uncertainty. Given the subject (suicide) and the audience, T5b must be plain and unsensational -- one sentence of fact, no dramatisation. Second rail: do not use the popular Mach 'Have you ever seen one?' jab as a quotation unless the build verifies a source -- present the energetics objection in the bank's own words instead. Third rail: the gravestone inscription is real, but the formula was cast in that exact form by Planck rather than written that way by Boltzmann -- verify and say it right. Dinner-test payoff: T1 (the egg that never unsmashes because of a count) with T2's gravestone as the image. Distractor mine: real rivals -- energetics/Ostwald, caloric (heat as an invisible fluid), the luminiferous ether, thermodynamics-without-atoms -- plus real names (Mach, Ostwald, Loschmidt, Zermelo, Planck, Perrin). Lane border: the arrow of time as a metaphysics seminar belongs to PHILOSOPHY; here it stays a physical count.

name: The Times corrects itself 49 years late
scope: A newspaper grades a physicist, then prints a retraction the morning after a Moon launch. T1: on 13 January 1920 the New York Times ran an unsigned editorial about physics professor Robert Goddard's claim that a rocket could reach the Moon, and informed its readers that he 'seems to lack the knowledge ladled out daily in high schools' (the hook: an anonymous editorial writer grading a working physicist on high-school science). T2: the editorial's specific error -- it argued that a rocket needs air to push against, so it could not work in the vacuum of space. The actual physics is Newton's third law: the rocket pushes the exhaust gas one way and the gas pushes the rocket the other, so air is not a requirement, it is a nuisance. A kid can settle it in ten seconds by letting go of an inflated balloon. T3: Goddard answered with hardware. On 16 March 1926, in a snowy field at his aunt Effie's farm in Auburn, Massachusetts, he launched the world's first liquid-fuelled rocket; his own diary records that it 'rose 41 feet & went 184 feet, in 2.5 secs.' Tiny -- and the ancestor of everything that followed. T4: the cost of the ridicule was secrecy. Goddard moved his work to Roswell, New Mexico, published sparingly and patented heavily -- multistage rockets, gyroscopic steering, gimballed thrust, turbopumps -- while other nations' rocket programmes advanced without him. T5a: on 17 July 1969, the day after Apollo 11 left the pad, the Times printed 'A Correction': 'Further investigation and experimentation have confirmed the findings of Isaac Newton in the 17th Century and it is now definitely established that a rocket can function in a vacuum as well as in an atmosphere. The Times regrets the error.' Goddard had been dead 24 years. T5b: the transferable rung -- the 1920 editorial was not stupid, it was CONFIDENT about a claim it had never tested, and the test was nearly free. Confidence and evidence are different things, and this is the one you can check yourself today.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_H._Goddard (13 January 1920 unsigned NYT editorial including the 'knowledge ladled out daily in high schools' line and the claim that a rocket's flight 'would be neither accelerated nor maintained by the explosion of the charges it then might have left'; the 16 March 1926 Auburn, Massachusetts liquid-fuelled flight with Goddard's diary figures of 41 feet, 184 feet, 2.5 seconds; the 17 July 1969 'A Correction' text verbatim, printed one day after the 16 July 1969 Apollo 11 launch). Grokipedia checked for this figure; corroboration above.
framing_note: REVERSAL keyed to the printed RETRACTION, plus a genuinely kid-replicable physics rung (the balloon) that lands the test-it-yourself soul. Accuracy rail: both the 1920 editorial line and the 1969 correction are documented and must be quoted verbatim; do NOT claim the Times apologised to Goddard personally (he died in 1945) and do NOT claim the 1926 rocket reached space -- it flew 41 feet up. Second rail: state the Roswell secrecy and the patent count only at the level the build can verify; do not inflate 'over 200 patents' without checking. Dinner-test payoff: T5a -- a 49-year-late newspaper correction, printed the morning after a Moon launch. Distractor mine: real period objections and real adjacent names -- Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, Hermann Oberth, Wernher von Braun, the 'rockets need air to push against' claim, the fuel-mass argument that the Moon was unreachable, Simon Newcomb's published argument that heavier-than-air flight was impossible. Lane border: Apollo as a Cold War story belongs to HISTORY; science owns the third-law physics, the 1926 flight and the correction.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank almost certainly covers the Space Race and Apollo 11 as a Cold War episode; this ladder must key the 1920 editorial, the 1926 Auburn flight and the 1969 printed correction, never the mission narrative or the Cold War politics.

name: Margulis, fifteen rejections, and the limit of being right
scope: A deliberately short ladder about what rejection proves and what vindication does not. T2: in 1967 a young Boston University biologist published a paper arguing that the powerhouses inside your cells were once free-living bacteria that got swallowed and never left -- after, by her own later account, roughly fifteen journals had turned the paper down; she published it as Lynn Sagan, in the Journal of Theoretical Biology. T4: the evidence that eventually turned the field: mitochondria and chloroplasts carry their OWN circular DNA and their own bacteria-style ribosomes, and they multiply by dividing on their own schedule rather than being assembled fresh from the nucleus's instructions. T5: the caveat rung, and the reason this ladder exists -- the same biologist later argued that cilia and flagella also descend from swallowed spirochete bacteria, and that claim has NOT been accepted. Being vindicated once does not make a person right the next time, and the bank never turns a vindicated heretic into an oracle.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Margulis ('On the Origin of Mitosing Cells', Journal of Theoretical Biology, 1967, published as Lynn Sagan; the paper 'rejected by about fifteen scientific journals' -- a figure traceable to her own account rather than editorial records; largely ignored for a further decade; acceptance in the early 1980s once mitochondrial and chloroplast genetic material was shown to differ from nuclear DNA; her spirochete origin of cilia and flagella still lacking mainstream acceptance). Grokipedia checked for this figure; corroboration above.
framing_note: MINI by design -- science's cell-biology strand owns endosymbiosis itself, so this ladder keys only the REJECTION and the LIMIT of vindication. Accuracy rail: the 'about fifteen rejections' number comes from Margulis's own later telling and must be attributed to her account, never stated as an audited record. Second rail: the T5 rung is MANDATORY -- the ladder is incomplete and off-voice without the rung showing that her later spirochete claim was rejected and stayed rejected. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (your mitochondria carry their own DNA). Distractor mine: the real rivals -- the autogenous hypothesis that organelles budded inward from the cell's own membranes, that the extra DNA was contamination, that organelles were viral in origin -- plus real names (Mereschkowsky, Ivan Wallin, Ris and Plaut). Lane border: the endosymbiosis MECHANISM and the organelle tour belong to science's cells strand; do not re-teach the organelle here, and coordinate so the cells strand keeps the mechanism while this ladder keeps the rejection.

name: Dismissed, then made into a unit
scope: A CONCEPT ladder across three men whose rejected work is now printed on instruments. T1: a schoolteacher in Cologne published in 1827 the relation every physics class now uses -- that the current through a conductor scales with the voltage across it -- and his own school thought so little of it that Georg Ohm resigned his post; his name is now stamped on every resistor as the unit of resistance. T2: Christian Doppler claimed in Prague in 1842 that a wave's pitch depends on whether its source is approaching or receding -- and got his own headline application wrong, since the colours of double stars are not explained by their motion at the speeds involved. The idea outlived the mistake. T3: the test that settled Doppler was gloriously physical: in 1845 the Dutch meteorologist Christophorus Buys Ballot ran the experiment on the railway line near Utrecht, putting musicians on an open car to hold a steady note while trained listeners on the ground wrote down the pitch they heard as the train approached and receded. The pitch dropped exactly as it passed. T4: Svante Arrhenius's 1884 Uppsala thesis -- that dissolved salt splits into charged ions in water all by itself, with no current applied -- so failed to impress his examiners that they graded it fourth class, raised to third only after his defence. The SAME theory took the 1903 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, with Ostwald, van 't Hoff and Clausius among the outsiders who saw its worth first. T5a: the pattern rung -- what these three share is not persecution but a GAP between a claim and the community's ability to test or use it: Ohm's law needed reliable batteries and galvanometers, Doppler's principle needed a source fast enough to hear, Arrhenius's ions needed physical chemistry to exist as a field at all. T5b: the naming rung -- a scientist's name becoming a UNIT (the ohm) or an EFFECT (the Doppler effect) is what vindication looks like once everyone has stopped arguing: the fight is forgotten and the name ends up printed on the instrument.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Ohm (1827 Die galvanische Kette, mathematisch bearbeitet; 'coldly received' in Germany; resignation from the Jesuit Gymnasium in Cologne; Nuremberg Polytechnic from 1833; Copley Medal 1841; Munich professorship 1852); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Doppler (1842 Prague paper 'Uber das farbige Licht der Doppelsterne...'; his own binary-star colour application later shown wrong; his mistaken belief about fast stars becoming invisible); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._H._D._Buys_Ballot (1845 test on the Utrecht line using musicians playing a calibrated note on a train); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svante_Arrhenius (1884 dissertation graded fourth class then reclassified third on defence; Uppsala professors including Cleve skeptical while Ostwald, van 't Hoff and Clausius were impressed; 1903 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for extensions of that same work; separate 1896 CO2 paper). Grokipedia checked for these figures; corroboration above.
framing_note: THEME ladder (shape B) -- three mini-gems on one analytic spine, so the sub-strand states its pattern rather than only anecdotalising it. Accuracy rails: (a) Arrhenius's thesis was graded FOURTH class and raised to THIRD at the defence -- never write 'it failed'; (b) Doppler's own starlight-colour application was WRONG and the ladder must say so, because a vindicated idea can still have a wrong original use; (c) the Buys Ballot test is verified as 1845 on the Utrecht line with musicians holding a calibrated note -- the specific 'trumpeters with perfect pitch' colour must be checked against Buys Ballot's own 1845 account before any rung asserts it; (d) do NOT use the Georg Friedrich Pohl 'web of naked fancies' line unless the build verifies a source; (e) Ohm's Munich chair was 1852, and the ohm was standardised internationally decades after his death -- verify the naming date before a rung uses it. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (a whole train hired to test one held note). Distractor mine: real adjacent names and rivals -- Volta, Ampere, Faraday, Fizeau (who independently applied the effect to light), van 't Hoff, Ostwald, Clausius, and the pre-Arrhenius view that ions could not exist without an applied current. Lane border: doing V=IR arithmetic belongs to MATH; here the wonder is the reception and the test. Keep Arrhenius's 1896 CO2 calculation OUT of this ladder -- it belongs to the climate strand.

name: What actually settles a scientific fight
scope: The analytic spine of the sub-strand: the anatomy of a real reversal, and why 'they laughed at Galileo' is not an argument. T2: the reversals in this bank do not run 'lone genius versus fools' -- they run CLAIM, then OBJECTION, then a TEST that could have come out either way, then verdict. Shechtman's tenfold pattern, Bretz's flood and Wegener's drift each ended when a new MEASUREMENT arrived, not when somebody won a debate. T3: the objection is usually the good part. Wegener had no mechanism; Prusiner's critics said the missing nucleic acid was a purification artifact; Eddington could not accept a star collapsing without limit. Two of those three were solid science, and naming the strongest thing said against a claim is a skill worth more than the anecdote. T4a: what a decisive test looks like -- it has to be able to FAIL. Mirror-image magnetic stripes on BOTH sides of a mid-ocean ridge; iridium concentrated in exactly one clay layer, worldwide; the pitch of a held note dropping as the train passes. Each had an outcome that would have killed the claim, which is what made the result worth anything. T4b: the 1980 case study -- Luis Alvarez, a physicist, and his son Walter, a geologist, with Frank Asaro and Helen Michel, found iridium (rare in Earth's crust, common in asteroids) spiked hundreds of times above background in the thin clay at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary at Gubbio in Italy, and proposed that an impact ended the dinosaurs. The reaction from paleontologists got personal enough that the episode is remembered as the dinosaur wars. T5a: how that case closed and what stayed open -- a buried crater roughly 180 km across at Chicxulub in Yucatan, dated to about 66 million years ago, was identified in 1991, and in 2010 a panel of 41 scientists reviewing twenty years of evidence endorsed the impact; the rival Deccan Traps volcanism explanation is still argued by researchers including Gerta Keller, and a combined impact-plus-eruption reading is live. An honest ladder says which part is closed and which is not. T5b: the asymmetry rung -- 'the consensus was wrong before, therefore my claim is right' is not an argument. For every Wegener there are many confident outsiders who were simply wrong: N-rays, polywater, cold fusion. What separates vindication from crankery is never defiance; it is a test other people can run that comes out the same way in their hands. T5c: the institutional rung -- in these cases the delay was rarely caused by wickedness. It was caused by ordinary machinery: a reigning theory quietly filtering what counts as data, an authority whose disapproval nobody would risk (Eddington), a discipline defending a hard-won rule (uniformitarianism), and journals declining what did not fit. Recognising the machinery is the point; indicting scientists is not.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvarez_hypothesis (1980 Science paper by Luis Alvarez, Walter Alvarez, Frank Asaro and Helen Vaughn Michel; iridium hundreds of times above background at the K-Pg boundary; iridium rare in Earth's crust and common in asteroids; Chicxulub crater in Yucatan as the impact site, impactor 10-15 km, ~66 Ma; the 2010 review by an international panel of 41 scientists endorsing the Chicxulub impact; Gerta Keller's continuing Deccan Traps advocacy and the synthesis proposal; the 'dinosaur wars' label and the unusually personal criticism). Cross-referenced with the sources for the Wegener, Chandrasekhar, Prusiner, Shechtman and Bretz ladders in this same sub-strand (Grokipedia pages for Alfred Wegener, Stanley B. Prusiner and Barbara McClintock; the Wikipedia pages listed in those specs). Primary for build stage: Alvarez, Alvarez, Asaro & Michel, Science 208 (1980); Schulte et al., Science 327 (2010).
framing_note: THE analytic backbone of the sub-strand and the ONLY spec here marked vision_mandated -- it carries the bank's 'consensus is not evidence' claim explicitly, so the moral audit must check it in BOTH directions: no smug anti-science sneer, and no whitewash of the institutional failures. The T5b asymmetry rung is MANDATORY and is what stops this sub-strand from teaching contrarianism-as-method; the T5c rung must explain the delays MECHANICALLY (theory filtering data, deference to authority, disciplinary rules, editorial gatekeeping), never moralise about scientists' characters. Accuracy rails: N-rays, polywater and cold fusion are real, documented failed claims that were tested and rejected -- name them accurately and never as joke options; state the Chicxulub diameter and date as approximate; and say plainly that the Deccan Traps contribution is still argued rather than presenting the case as fully shut (MYSTERY discipline: never let a distractor secretly be the truth). Dinner-test payoff: T4b (a father-and-son team read a mass extinction out of one thin clay layer). Distractor mine: real rival extinction explanations serious scientists held -- gradual sea-level fall, long-term climate cooling, Deccan volcanism, disease, mammals eating the eggs -- plus real names (Alvarez, Asaro, Michel, Keller, Hildebrand, Penfield). Lane border: falsifiability as a PHILOSOPHY seminar -- Popper's demarcation, Kuhn's paradigms -- belongs to the philosophy bank; this ladder stays on working practice, i.e. what a test that can fail actually looks like on a ship, in a clay layer, or on a railway platform. Cross-strand: it may REFERENCE Semmelweis and Marshall as pattern instances but must not build a rung on their facts (they live in the germ-theory and medicine strands).
history_overlap: ANIMAL bank may cover dinosaurs and the end-Cretaceous extinction as a creature story, and GEOGRAPHY may cover the Chicxulub crater or the Yucatan as a place -- this ladder must key the iridium evidence, the hostile reception and the 1991 crater identification, not the dinosaurs or the site tour. Also check PHILOSOPHY's reasoning ladders for an existing falsifiability/Popper rung before authoring the T4a test rung.
